source: Anglo-Saxon futhorc — meanings for runes 1–29 drawn from the Old English Rune Poem (historical); Cweorth, Calc, Stan, Gar per Northumbrian manuscript tradition (no poem stanzas)
note: Gyfu, Haegl, Is, Eoh, Sigel, Ing, Ethel and Daeg are symmetric and traditionally read the same face-up or face-down; their merkstave is null.

upright.meaning: Wealth is a comfort to all — yet the poem bids every man bestow it freely, for it must leave his grasp. Prosperity that circulates.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: wealth clutched till it sours. Greed, or resources slipping through closed fingers.

upright.meaning: The aurochs — proud, great-horned, very savage. Untamed vitality; the wild strength that bows to no master.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the wild ox yoked or spent. Vitality drained; do not mistake exhaustion for peace.

upright.meaning: The thorn — exceedingly sharp, an evil thing for any knight to touch, yet every thorn guards a rose. A sharp trial; defense that wounds.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the thorn turned inward. Defensive cruelty, or a trial made sharper by your own hand.

upright.meaning: The mouth — source of all language, pillar of wisdom, comfort of the wise. The spoken word rightly wielded.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the mouth as snare. Empty speech, flattery, or wisdom withheld when it was needed.

upright.meaning: Riding — easy to the warrior indoors, and courageous on the high road astride a stout horse. The journey taken at the right pace.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the rider astray. Haste without rhythm, or a road that only looks right from indoors.

upright.meaning: The torch — known to every living man by its pale bright flame, burning where princes sit within. Clarity; revelation that shows the hall as it is.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the torch gutters. False clarity, or light that burns the bearer — rest the flame.

upright.meaning: Generosity — the gift that brings credit and honour and upholds dignity. Given freely, it binds giver and receiver in honor.
Bliss — joy to him who knows little of woe, who has prosperity and happiness and a good enough house. Harmony; the reward of right living.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: joy's shadow. Sorrow, or happiness built on sand — check what the bliss is standing on.

upright.meaning: Hail — whitest of grain, whirled from heaven's vault by gusts of wind, then melting to water. Sudden trial from above; it passes, and waters what follows.
Trouble — oppressive to the heart, yet often it proves a source of help and salvation, if heeded in time. Hardship that teaches.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: trouble unheeded till it hardens. Despair, or the help that was offered too late.

upright.meaning: Ice — very cold and immeasurably slippery, glittering like gems over the field. All things suspended in bright stillness.
Harvest — summer's joy, when the holy King of Heaven lets the earth bring forth shining fruits for rich and poor. The season honored; reaping in its time.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: sowing against the season. Impatience, or the harvest left to rot in the field.

upright.meaning: The yew — rough-barked, hard and fast in the earth, the bow-tree. Endurance rooted deep; flexibility that does not break.
The dice-cup — recreation and amusement where warriors sit blithely in the beerhall. Play, fellowship, the honest gamble.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: play curdles. The gamble that stops being honest — know when to leave the hall.

upright.meaning: The elk-sedge of the marsh — it grows in water and makes a ghastly wound on any hand that grasps it. Defense by position; the ground itself fights for you.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the marsh traps its defender. A refuge that becomes a snare — choose your ground.

upright.meaning: The sun — ever a joy in the hopes of seafarers journeying over the fishes' bath, till the sea-horse brings them to land. Victory; the light that guides home.
Tir the star — it keeps faith with princes, ever on its course over night's mists and never failing. Honor as navigation; the fixed point.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the star obscured. Faith broken or bearings lost — steer by something smaller and nearer.

upright.meaning: The birch — bearing no fruit, yet bringing forth suckers without seed, bright-branched and lovely. Growth from unexpected shoots; renewal.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: shoots that will not take. Effort without fruit — tend the roots, not the branches.

upright.meaning: The horse — joy of princes before warriors, the mettled steed proud on its hooves. Trust between rider and ridden; partnership that carries.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the horse shies. Trust strained, or a partnership pulling in two directions.

upright.meaning: Man — dear to his kinsmen, yet every man is doomed to fail his fellow, for the Lord's decree takes the wretched flesh to earth. Kinship, and its limits.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: kinship fails. Betrayal, or the loneliness of the one no kin will claim.

upright.meaning: The ocean — interminable to those who venture on the rolling bark, whom the briny waves frighten and the sea-horse heeds not. The deep road; surrender to the flow.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the sea takes. Overwhelm — do not sail till the weather turns.

upright.meaning: Ing — first seen among the East-Danes, departing eastward over the waves in his chariot, the Wagoner following. The seed-god; potential held in the dark, waiting.
The estate — very dear to every man who may enjoy in his house whatever is right and proper in constant prosperity. Homeland; rightful dwelling.
Day — the glorious light of the Creator, sent by the Lord, beloved of men, a joy and hope to rich and poor. Breakthrough; the dawn that ends every night.
The oak — fattening the pigs' flesh for heroes, often traversing the gannet's bath to try the ocean. Strength that feeds others; endurance tested by the sea.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the oak that will not bend. Strength turned to rigidity — what cannot flex will break.

upright.meaning: The ash — very tall and precious to men, hard on its base, holding its place though many attack it. Stature; the tree that holds the worlds.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the tall tree with shallow roots. Pride before the felling — deepen, or fall.

upright.meaning: Yr — joy and honour to prince and knight, looking well on a horse, steady gear on a journey. The bow: craft aimed true.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the bow unstrung or misaimed. Craft without aim, or gear failing on the road.

upright.meaning: Ior — the river-fish that takes its food on land, at home in both elements. The between-creature: duality held without tearing.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the between becomes the trap. Torn by two elements, at home in neither — choose a shore.

upright.meaning: The grave — horrible to every knight when the corpse quickly begins to cool and is laid in the darkness. Ending; the dust that claims all flesh. Mourn, then release.

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the grave clung to. An ending refused till it rots — bury it and walk on.

upright.meaning: The fire-drill — the Northumbrian rune of sacred fire, kindled by friction. Transformation through effort; the hearth lit by will. (No rune-poem stanza; manuscript tradition.)

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: fire without hearth. Wildfire, or the self burned out by its own kindling.

upright.meaning: The chalice — the Northumbrian cup-rune. Offering poured out; the vessel that holds blessing. (No rune-poem stanza; manuscript tradition.)

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the cup overturned. Offerings wasted, or the vessel cracked — mend it before pouring.

upright.meaning: The stone — the Northumbrian rune of what endures. Foundation, landmark, the altar-stone. (No rune-poem stanza; manuscript tradition.)

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: foundation on sand. What seemed stone sinks — test the ground before building.

upright.meaning: The spear — the Northumbrian rune of Gár, the god's own weapon. The direct hit; force aimed by higher hands. (No rune-poem stanza; manuscript tradition.)

merkstave.meaning: Murk-stave: the spear thrown amiss. Force misdirected — or aimed at you. Duck, or aim better.
